label: lem:write_correct
title: Correctness of a write
statement:
Let $i\ge 2$ and let $p$ be a prime such that $p \le \mathrm{lp}(i)$.
    Then $p$ is the least prime factor of $ip$.
proof: Since $p$ is prime and $p \mid ip$, it suffices to show no prime $q < p$ divides $ip$. Any such $q$ would divide $i$ (since $q < p$ and $p$ is prime), contradicting $p \le \mathrm{lp}(i)$.
